name: Congenital Pseudoarthrosis of the Fibula

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Radiographic Diagnostic Criteria for Congenital Pseudoarthrosis of the Fibula

criteria.description: Radiographic evidence of fibular nonunion or pseudoarthrosis present at birth or early infancy
Visible deformity or angulation of the fibula with limb length discrepancy
No history of trauma or fracture explaining the fibular nonunion
Presence of neurofibromatosis type 1 features (in some cases)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of radiographic fibular pseudoarthrosis and clinical deformity with exclusion of traumatic causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical and radiographic; genetic testing may be supportive if NF1 is suspected.

searchTerms: birth defect causing false joint in fibula

common.symptomName: Limb length discrepancy of the affected lower extremity
searchTerms: leg length difference in lower limb

common.symptomName: Tibial bowing or deformity associated with fibular pseudoarthrosis
searchTerms: bowed shin bone with fibula problem
tibia deformity linked to fibular pseudoarthrosis

common.symptomName: Localized swelling or mass at the site of pseudoarthrosis
searchTerms: swelling or lump at false joint

common.symptomName: Difficulty with weight-bearing or gait abnormalities

occasional.symptomName: Pain localized to the fibular pseudoarthrosis site
searchTerms: pain at fibula false joint site
pain in lower leg pseudoarthrosis area

occasional.symptomName: Cutaneous café-au-lait spots (if associated with NF1)
searchTerms: pigmented skin marks associated with NF1

occasional.symptomName: Neurofibroma formation near the affected limb (in NF1-associated cases)
Muscle atrophy of the affected lower limb
searchTerms: loss of muscle bulk in leg
fibula bone fractures that heal poorly

rare.symptomName: Neurovascular compromise in the affected limb
searchTerms: nerve and blood vessel problems in leg
circulation and nerve issues in limb

imaging: X-ray showing fibular nonunion with pseudoarthrosis
MRI to assess soft tissue and neurofibroma involvement if NF1 suspected
CT scan for detailed bone architecture evaluation
genetic: Genetic testing for NF1 gene mutations if neurofibromatosis type 1 is suspected
other: Clinical examination revealing limb deformity and discrepancy
Histopathology of pseudoarthrosis tissue may show fibrous tissue and abnormal periosteum

distinguishingFeatures: Involvement primarily of the tibia rather than fibula
More frequent association with neurofibromatosis type 1
Higher risk of pathological fractures and deformity
History of trauma or fracture preceding nonunion
Absence of congenital deformity at birth
Radiographic evidence of fracture healing attempts

redFlags: Signs of neurovascular compromise in the affected limb
